outcome: Nothing has moved this question since 26 January 2024: whether 2^ℵ_ω < ℵ_ω1 when ℵ_ω is a strong limit remains open, Shelah's ℵ_ω4 bound is unchanged, the only in-window paper that bounds the continuum at singular cardinals (Garti, May 2024) does not reach ℵ_ω, and no AI-involved result on this question was found.
problem_asks: (1) Hypothesis: ℵ_ω is a strong limit cardinal (so 2^ℵ_n < ℵ_ω for every n). (2) Question: is 2^ℵ_ω < ℵ_ω1, i.e. is the continuum at ℵ_ω below the ω_1-th aleph? The answer sought is yes or no. Not asked by this bullet: whether ℵ_ω4 is optimal, and the related pp(ℵ_ω) < ℵ_ω1 form, which Shelah discusses in the same source but which is not in this bullet. The Wikipedia parenthetical 'see Singular cardinals hypothesis' is context, and its second sentence (Shelah's ℵ_ω4 bound) is context, not an ask.

events.what_happened: Shelah's pcf theory gives, for strong limit ℵ_ω, the upper bounds 2^ℵ_ω < ℵ_ω4 and 2^ℵ_ω < ℵ_(2^ℵ_0)^+. The argument: if ℵ_4 ≤ |pcf{ℵ_n : n<ω}| then a certain structure exists on ω_4, which is then shown impossible. The earliest written statement I opened is Jech and Shelah, 'Possible pcf algebras' (arXiv math/9412208, posted 3 Dec 1994; J. Symbolic Logic 61 (1996) 313-317), whose introduction says Shelah 'proved, among others' both bounds and that the ω_4 bound 'is established via an analysis of the structure of pcf'. Garti (arXiv 2405.03142, 2024) cites the result as [She94], Shelah's Cardinal Arithmetic (Oxford Logic Guides 29, 1994). Shelah's expository survey 'Cardinal arithmetic for skeptics' (arXiv math/9201251, Jan 1992) is the earliest source I found; its abstract only says it surveys pcf applications, and I did not verify the ω_4 argument in it. The date is therefore year-only and may be earlier than the first written argument, which I could not pin down.
events.revisions: Jech-Shelah math/9412208: one version (v1, 3 Dec 1994) per the arXiv abstract page; journal version JSL 61 (1996). Garti restates the bound in 2024.
events.delivers: For strong limit ℵ_ω: 2^ℵ_ω < ℵ_ω4, and 2^ℵ_ω < ℵ_(2^ℵ_0)^+, so 2^ℵ_ω is below the smaller of the two. Restricted to the case ℵ_ω strong limit; no statement about ℵ_ω1 as a bound.
events.remains: The whole question: 2^ℵ_ω < ℵ_ω1 is not established. Jech-Shelah also record that it is unknown whether the index 4 can be reduced (search summary of the paper; not verified in the full text).

checked_by.what_they_did: Textbook exposition of the pcf bound. Not opened by me: the PDF returned undecodable binary to WebFetch, so this is cited from a search result only.

checked_by.what_they_did: Standard expository treatment of Shelah's bound, cited in search results as the reference for the argument. Not located or opened by me.

events.doubts: No source I opened disputes the bound. Two points of wording: (a) the Wikipedia phrase 'the best bound, ℵ_ω4' does not hold uniformly, because ℵ_(2^ℵ_0)^+ is smaller whenever 2^ℵ_0 < ℵ_3, so the usable bound depends on the continuum; (b) search summaries of Shelah's 1999 survey say he regarded ℵ_ω4 as possibly the right bound but doubted it is the right question, and that the index is not known to be optimal. Neither is a challenge to the bound itself.
events.direction: Upper bound on the same quantity the question asks about, 2^ℵ_ω, but at index ω_4 (and at (2^ℵ_0)^+), not ω_1. It answers neither way on the question asked. It is not a counterexample and exhibits no object.

events.what_happened: Not a result. Shelah states the bullet's question as Question 1.4(1) of 'On what I do not understand (and have something to say), Part I' (arXiv math/9906113; posted 16 June 1999; Fund. Math. 166 (2000) 1-82): 'Assume ℵ_ω is strong limit. Is 2^ℵ_ω < ℵ_ω1?' He notes that under strong limit 2^ℵ_ω = (ℵ_ω)^ℵ_0 and, per the fetched summary, treats Question 1.4(1), Question 1.4(2) and pp(ℵ_ω) < ℵ_ω1 as equivalent. Recorded here because it is the source of the open status and it fixes the question's wording; it is not a claim about the answer.
events.revisions: v1 only per arXiv abstract page; journal Fund. Math. 166 (2000).
events.direction: Not applicable: a question, not a claim about the answer.

events.what_happened: Consistency results on the lower side. Woodin's argument, as presented by Golshani (arXiv 1601.04141, 16 Jan 2016): from a (κ+2)-strong cardinal κ, a generic extension in which κ = ℵ_ω, GCH holds below ℵ_ω, and 2^ℵ_ω = ℵ_(ω+2). Since GCH below ℵ_ω gives 2^ℵ_n < ℵ_ω for all n, ℵ_ω is strong limit there (my inference). Search summaries also report Magidor and Shelah models with 2^ℵ_ω = ℵ_(ω+k+1) and ℵ_(ω+α+1), and cite arXiv math/0406441 for the latter; I did not open those.
events.revisions: Golshani 1601.04141: v1 only. The date is that of the exposition I opened, not of Woodin's original argument, which I did not find.
events.delivers: Consistency of ℵ_ω strong limit with 2^ℵ_ω = ℵ_(ω+2), relative to a (κ+2)-strong cardinal. A lower-side consistency result only.
events.remains: Whether 2^ℵ_ω can reach ℵ_ω1 while ℵ_ω is strong limit. The model reaches only ℵ_(ω+2), which is below ℵ_ω1.

checked_by.qualification: Set theorist; author of the exposition
checked_by.what_they_did: Wrote an exposition presenting Woodin's proof. I read the abstract only, not the body.

events.direction: Moves the lower end of the possible values of 2^ℵ_ω (above ℵ_(ω+1)), not the upper bound. Does not bear on whether it is below ℵ_ω1.

events.what_happened: Shimon Garti, 'Weak diamond and pcf theory' (arXiv 2405.03142, posted 6 May 2024, in the window). Under weak-diamond-type hypotheses it gives: |pcf(𝔞)| < |𝔞|^+3 for progressive 𝔞; and 2^ℵ_δ < ℵ_(|δ|^+3) for a class ℭ of singular cardinals ℵ_δ. Theorem 3.3 assumes every limit cardinal is strong limit and concludes for ℵ_δ in a class ℭ; Corollary 3.2 is for strong limit, non-fixed-point λ = ℵ_δ under 2^(η+) < 2^(η++). The introduction restates the ℵ_ω case as 'Shelah's theorem in the specific case of ℵω amounts to 2ℵω<ℵω4', calls it the current bound, and says 2^ℵω < ℵω1 holds in all known models of the failure of SCH at ℵω. The paper does not state that ℵ_ω belongs to ℭ.
events.revisions: v1 only (6 May 2024) per the arXiv abstract page as fetched on 12 Oct 2026. No journal version found.
events.delivers: 2^ℵ_δ < ℵ_(|δ|^+3) for singular ℵ_δ in a class ℭ, under the stated hypotheses (every limit cardinal strong limit, or 2^(η+) < 2^(η++) for a strong limit non-fixed-point cardinal). For δ = ω the paper gives no bound; the paper's own introduction records the unconditional ℵ_ω bound as ℵ_ω4.
events.remains: The whole question for ℵ_ω: 2^ℵ_ω < ℵ_ω1 is not addressed. Whether ℵ_ω ∈ ℭ is not established by the paper.
events.doubts: (a) The bound is conditional on hypotheses that are not shown to hold at ℵ_ω; reading it as an ℵ_ω improvement needs ℵ_ω ∈ ℭ, which the paper does not state. (b) The fetched text quotes the author saying he 'actually believe[s] that the main result is provable in ZFC', so he regards the hypotheses as removable; that belief is not a result. (c) No journal version or public engagement found in my searches.
events.direction: Lowers the index from |δ|^+4 to |δ|^+3 for a class of singular cardinals under hypotheses. For ℵ_ω it changes nothing that the paper establishes, and it does not reach ℵ_ω1 on any reading.

events.what_happened: Hannes Jakob and Maxwell Levine, 'Failure of Approachability at the Successor of the first Singular for any Cofinality' (arXiv 2503.18898, posted 24 Mar 2025, in the window). Consistency with GCH that for every n ≥ 1 some stationary set of points of cofinality ℵ_n lies outside the approachability ideal I[ℵ_(ω+1)]; corollary: goodness and approachability differ for stationarily many points of cofinality ℵ_1. The abstract and text I read do not discuss 2^ℵ_ω or give any bound on it.
events.revisions: v1 24 Mar 2025; v2 6 Oct 2025 (current), per arXiv abstract page.
events.delivers: Consistency results about approachability at ℵ_(ω+1). Nothing about the continuum at ℵ_ω.
events.direction: Not about this question. Search summaries say Shelah's ω_4 argument uses good and approachable points; I did not verify that from the paper.

events.what_happened: Hannes Jakob and Alejandro Poveda, 'On Shelah's Approachability Ideal' (arXiv 2508.04374, posted 6 Aug 2025, in the window). For a singular ℵ_γ and regular μ, under large cardinal assumptions, a ZFC model in which ℵ_(γ+1) ∩ cof(μ) is not in the approachability ideal I[ℵ_(γ+1)], and a model in which approachability fails at every singular cardinal. Neither the abstract nor the fetched text mentions 2^ℵ_ω, the continuum at ℵ_ω, or ℵ_ω1.
events.revisions: v1 only per arXiv abstract page (submitted by Poveda).
events.delivers: Consistency results on the approachability ideal at successors of singular cardinals. Nothing about the continuum.

events.what_happened: Tom Benhamou and Dima Sinapova, 'Stationary Reflection and the Failure of SCH at ℵ_ω1' (arXiv 2411.09048, posted 13 Nov 2024, in the window; v2 24 Nov 2024 fixes typos). From uncountably many supercompact cardinals: consistency of ℵ_ω1 being strong limit, 2^ℵ_ω1 > ℵ_(ω1+1), and reflection of all stationary subsets of ℵ_(ω1+1). The singular cardinal in question is ℵ_ω1, not ℵ_ω.
events.revisions: v1 13 Nov 2024; v2 24 Nov 2024 ('corrected some typos').
events.delivers: A consistency result about ℵ_ω1 (strong limit, with 2^ℵ_ω1 > ℵ_(ω1+1)). It is about a different cardinal from this bullet and does not bear on 2^ℵ_ω.
events.direction: Not about this question. Recorded because the cardinal ℵ_ω1 and the bullet's ℵ_ω1 are easy to confuse: here ℵ_ω1 is the singular cardinal, and the bullet uses it as the bound.

summary: The Wikipedia entry was confirmed verbatim from the Set theory section of the frozen-era page (fetched in three chunks): 'If ℵω is a strong limit cardinal, is 2^ℵω < ℵω1 (see Singular cardinals hypothesis)? The best bound, ℵω4, was obtained by Shelah using his PCF theory.' The question is Shelah's own: Question 1.4(1) of 'On what I do not understand, Part I' (arXiv math/9906113, June 1999, Fund. Math. 2000), which I read via its HTML rendering; the PDF was undecodable. The upper bound is in Jech and Shelah, 'Possible pcf algebras' (arXiv math/9412208, Dec 1994), which states that if ℵω is strong limit then 2^ℵω < ℵ_(2^ℵ0)^+ and 2^ℵω < ℵω4; so 'the best bound' is not uniformly the best, since the first bound is smaller whenever 2^ℵ0 < ℵ3. Garti (arXiv 2405.03142, 6 May 2024, v1 only, no journal version found) is the only paper in the window that bounds 2^ℵδ at singular cardinals. Read in full in its HTML form, it gives 2^ℵδ < ℵ_(|δ|^+3) for a class ℭ of singular cardinals under hypotheses; its introduction restates the ℵω case as the ω_4 bound and says the question remains a major open problem, so the paper does not reach ℵω and is discounted here, while being the closest in-window candidate for a move. Other in-window papers (Jakob–Levine, Jakob–Poveda on approachability; Benhamou–Sinapova on ℵ_ω1) are about other questions and are recorded as discounted events. The Woodin lower-bound model (Golshani's exposition, 2016) is also recorded and does not bear on ℵ_ω1. The author-listing checks found no 2024–2026 Shelah preprint on pcf or ℵ_ω: the 2026 items (homogeneous forcing; super black boxes; HJ numbers; square-bracket partition relations) were opened and none concerns this question. No checked claim of settlement or of a new bound was found. Checking: no entry in the full OpenAI 'openai/math' catalogue (released 6 Oct 2026; 719 manuscripts; unnamed internal model) concerns ℵω, singular cardinals, pcf or the continuum; set-theory-adjacent entries (240 on Shelah's eventual categoricity, 243, 244, 297, 323) are other problems. The Erdős AI wiki (data to 30 June 2026) has no entry identified as set theory; its Shelah-cited entry #1036 is a graph-theory problem. The first AI-solved FrontierMath Open Problem (Brian–Larson hypergraph, 23 March 2026, GPT-5.4 Pro) is a Ramsey-type hypergraph problem, not this one. No system was credited with work on this bullet in any source I opened, and the more than a dozen AI-specific searches surfaced nothing relevant. Close calls, both recorded not resolved: (i) whether the Wikipedia 'best bound' wording should make ℵω4 the reference bound; (ii) whether Garti's Theorem 3.3 applies to ℵω, which the paper does not say.
competing_reading: Read Garti's Theorem 3.3 as covering ℵ_ω: under 'every limit cardinal is strong limit' the bound at ℵ_ω would drop from ℵ_ω4 to ℵ_ω3, an in-window improvement of the index, though still not to ℵ_ω1 and conditional on a hypothesis that the question does not assume. On that reading the record shows a move, and an event that the later pass would weigh; on the reading I took (the paper does not state ℵ_ω ∈ ℭ, and its own introduction keeps ℵ_ω4 as the bound) there is no move. Either way the ℵ_ω1 question is unaffected.
what_would_settle_it: For the question as asked: a ZFC proof that 2^ℵ_ω < ℵ_ω1 when ℵ_ω is strong limit (affirmative), or a forcing model with ℵ_ω strong limit and 2^ℵ_ω ≥ ℵ_ω1 (negative). Equivalent pcf form: a proof of pp(ℵ_ω) < ℵ_ω1, which Shelah's Part I treats as equivalent. For Garti: whether ℵ_ω satisfies the hypotheses of Theorem 3.3 or Corollary 3.2, and whether the author's stated belief that the result is provable in ZFC holds up. For the classical bound: the text of Shelah's Cardinal Arithmetic (1994) and the Abraham–Magidor chapter, which I could not open, to confirm the ω_4 argument and its exact hypotheses.

judgement.why: Shelah's ℵ_ω4 bound (1994, pre-snapshot) is a bound on the asked quantity, digested via the JSL-published Jech–Shelah paper and standard textbook expositions. Shelah's 1999 paper only poses the question. The Woodin/Golshani model is a consistency result well below ℵ_ω1 that neither bounds nor settles the question: none. Garti (May 2024) is the only close call: its |δ|^+3 bound holds under extra hypotheses (weak-diamond / every limit strong limit) and the paper neither states that ℵ_ω is in its class ℭ nor claims an ℵ_ω improvement, its own introduction keeping ℵ_ω4 — so it answers a changed question (variant) rather than moving this bound; the competing reading would make it a conditional bound still on different hypotheses, which is a variant either way. Benhamou–Sinapova concerns the singular ℵ_ω1, a different cardinal (variant); the approachability papers do not address the continuum (none). No AI involvement anywhere.
judgement.doubts: The 1994 date is year-only and possibly later than Shelah's first written argument; either way it is pre-snapshot. Expert expositions of the bound (Jech ch. 24, Abraham–Magidor) were cited from search snippets, not opened, but the journal publication of Jech–Shelah suffices.
